blocks.text:
# gh-740: [GOAL] Compaction failure must never brick a session — deterministic trim fallback, decorrelated role chain, trap circuit-breaker (M1 spec: 90s→300s ready)

## Description

## Goal — compaction failure must never brick a session (v1, full create-goal rewrite)

One sentence: **a session whose summarizers all fail still continues** — a deterministic no-model fallback frees the window, the trap loop breaks itself, and steering queued during the wedge delivers on recovery.

Owner transcript (CLI 0.1.432, dmtools-dart session, ctx 262k/262k): mid-run the window exhausts → «request was not sent; auto-compacting…» → **both** compaction roles die with the IDENTICAL `TimeoutException after 0:01:30 — structured compaction checkpoint summarizer exceeded the 90s budget (issue #515)` → «the agent cannot make progress until you switch models or /new» → the owner types `continue` → the same over-window → same compaction → same 90s double-timeout, loop forever; steering piles up undelivered, the run is declared stalled. Only manual model surgery or `/new` escapes. Why now: this is the third brick-by-compaction report in this family (#515, #541 closed — yet the trap is still reachable), and it hit a real work session with 5 completed edits in flight.

## Why this framing
- «Can't continue session» is retracted as a vague bug: the transcript shows THREE distinct defects compounding — (a) both roles failing to the SAME cause (the fallback chain collapses instead of diversifying), (b) no deterministic no-model escape hatch on this path despite #541's fallback work, (c) a trap loop that re-runs the same failing compaction on every message and never offers a working exit.

## RCA (code-traced on main @ 0.1.434)

- `onBothRolesFailed` (agent_cli_compaction.dart:197) prints the dead-end pair of lines; `_compactionFailureHint` only special-cases usage-limit/429 — a **timeout** gets no actionable hint, and the advice «/model» points at the CHAT model while compaction rides `roles.smol` — misdirected recovery.
- The attempt budget (#515; 90s at report time — **mitigation M1 below raises the default to 300s, not yet landed**) applies uniformly: for a 262k-token checkpoint on a slow provider, EVERY role attempt hits the same wall at the same time — the chain fails correlated, by construction.
- The deterministic local-trim fallback (`_localTrimFallback`, auto_compactor) did not save this session — either not reached on the structured-checkpoint path or insufficient against 100% fill; «could not free the context window» is the symptom.
- Steering during the trap is correctly PERSISTED (#437/#488 family works) but can never be DELIVERED, because delivery needs a run that can make progress — and progress needs the compaction that just failed.

## Fix contract

1. **Deterministic escape hatch, always.** When every summarizer role fails, a no-model local trim (keep system + recent working set, route through the pairing repairer) frees the window and the run CONTINUES — lossy, loud (one named notice), but the session is never bricked by a summarizer outage. No config, no opt-in: this is the floor.
2. **Decorrelated failure.** The roles chain must diversify: per-attempt budget escalation (the fallback role gets a larger budget — the knob EXISTS: `compaction.judgeBudgetSeconds` (#541), now defaulting to 300s; make it adaptive to checkpoint size), and two attempts dying to the identical cause never counts as «both roles failed» without a structurally different path tried (trim included).
3. **Circuit breaker.** After N consecutive compaction failures in one run, the loop stops re-entering compaction on every message and presents ONE actionable recovery row (switch `roles.smol` / force local trim / new session) — no more silent re-fail per «continue».
4. **Honest recovery copy.** The failure hint names `roles.smol`, `compaction.judgeBudgetSeconds`, and `/settings → Agent models` for ALL failure classes (timeout included), never «/model» of the chat model.
5. **Steering delivers on recovery.** Whatever the owner steered during the wedge delivers into the first successful post-recovery turn (the persisted FIFO already exists — wire it).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)
- **AC1** (RED, IT): scripted over-window session, fake smol stream that ALWAYS times out → deterministic trim engages, the run completes a turn, one loud notice printed. (IT-E1)
- **AC2** (IT): owner transcript replay — `continue` after double-timeout reaches the agent after recovery; no infinite compact-fail loop (circuit breaker opens after N, recovery row shown). (IT-E2, IT-E3)
- **AC3** (UT): timeout-class error → hint names `roles.smol`; identical-cause collapse routes to trim, never a bare double-fail declaration. (UT-H1, UT-D1)
- **AC4** (REG): #541 (judge SPOF), #673 (mid-turn crash), #515, #438 (badge) suites green — *red REG blocks merge*.

## Test plan
- `UT-H1/UT-D1` pure hint/chain logic; `IT-E1..E3` fake-provider scripted sessions, deterministic clocks (90s budget simulated); `REG-*` the named suites. Edge cases: **E1** trim still insufficient (genuinely oversized single record → #729's payload-fit path, cross-ref); **E2** owner switches smol mid-trap — breaker resets, next compaction retried fresh; **E3** manual `/compact` in the trap uses the same fallback ladder, not a separate one; **E4** trim during a tool-call phase — pairing repair keeps the active call chain intact (#85).

## Non-goals
- Making the summarizer faster (provider/role tuning is the owner's config).
- #729's payload-window-fit work (sibling card — this one assumes it, doesn't duplicate it).
- Changing the structured-compaction format itself.


## Immediate mitigation (lands first — spec ready for the worker)

**M1 — raise the attempt budget default 90s → 300s** (owner decision 2026-09-20; analysis + exact edit list verified locally, reverted — no code committed by the orchestrator):
- `lib/src/compaction/structured/engine.dart` — `attemptBudget` default `Duration(seconds: 90)` → 300;
- `lib/src/agent/auto_compactor.dart` — BOTH defaults (compactor ctor + judge/config ctor) 90 → 300;
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_compaction.dart` — resolver `compactionJudgeBudgetSeconds ?? 90` → `?? 300` (+ comment);
- comment sweep: «90s default/cap» → 300s in `auto_compactor.dart` (rationale + `onAttemptStart` doc), `compaction/compaction_engine.dart`, `cli_config.dart` (×2), `agent_cli_config.dart`;
- test: `test/agent/auto_compactor_test.dart` — «default budgets are tight — 90 s per attempt» → 300 s (name + expectation);
- the `compaction.judgeBudgetSeconds` knob (#541) is unchanged and keeps overriding;
- verified: `dart analyze` clean; `auto_compactor_test` + `structured_judge_fallback_test` 22/22 green with the change applied.

**M2 — commit-time hazards found while gating (fix or route around):**
- `dart analyze` scans ALL of the package root: stale untracked leftovers `tool/profile_boot.dart` + `tool/hub_probe.dart` (dangling refs to renamed APIs) fail the gate with 2 errors — delete or gitignore them;
- `test/cli/fah_hub_serve_dispatch_test.dart`: 5 tests («nothing stored/no terminal», «live hub idempotent», «taken port» ×2, «unwritable pid path») FAIL deterministically under the hook's full-suite parallel run on the owner's macOS machine (port contention: «shared flag to bind() needs to be true if binding multiple times») but pass 19/19 standalone — a test-isolation bug that currently blocks EVERY hook-gated commit on this machine; quarantine or serialize before landing M1 through the hook.

## Open questions
- N for the circuit breaker (lean: 2 consecutive double-failures).
- Should the forced local trim ASK first (approval-style) or just act with a loud notice? (Lean: act — a bricked session is worse than a lossy trim; the notice says what was dropped.)

## References
#515 (90s budget origin), #541 (judge SPOF fallback — same class, closed), #673 (mid-turn compaction crash), #729 (compaction payload must fit window), #437/#488 (steering persistence), #85 (pairing repair), owner transcript: CLI 0.1.432, dmtools-dart, 2026-09-20.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ╔═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
# ║  QUALITY GATE — DO NOT LOWER THESE THRESHOLDS WITHOUT TEAM APPROVAL       ║
# ║  Every commit must pass: file size, analyze, tests, coverage ≥ 80%,       ║
# ║  CRAP ratchet (crap4dart.yaml), duplication < 1%.                         ║
# ╚═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
#
# Pre-commit hook for flutter_agent_harness (pure Dart package).
# Canonical copy: scripts/pre-commit — install with:
#   cp scripts/pre-commit .git/hooks/pre-commit && chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-commit
# To skip (emergency only): git commit --no-verify
#
# Issue #177 (AC7): the hook is a THIN WRAPPER over scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh —
# the exact script CI runs — with the same path filters: a docs-only commit
# no longer pays for the flutter suite, a lib-only commit skips flutter_app
# stages. Hook-specific extras that stay here (they make no sense in CI):
#   1. dart format SELF-HEAL of staged files (reformat + re-stage, blocking
#      backstop when the formatter can't),
#   2. the golden-coverage quick check (check_goldens.py --quick) — local
#      golden hygiene; pixel goldens themselves run inside the gate's
#      flutter stage.
# Parity check: both callers print `GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP <reason>`
# markers; diffing the hook's markers against CI's must be empty.

set -euo pipefail

cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"

echo "🎨 Auto-formatting staged Dart files..."
# Format is SELF-HEALING with a BLOCKING backstop: reformat exactly the
# Dart files in the index and re-stage them; anything still unformatted
# after that (formatter crashed on syntax errors) blocks the commit with a
# clear message. A whole-tree `--set-exit-if-changed` gate both (a) failed
# commits over a single unformatted line and (b) rewrote OTHER agents'
# work-in-progress files mid-edit when run concurrently — scoped auto-fix
# avoids both.
STAGED_DART=$(git diff --cached --name-only --diff-filter=ACM | grep '\.dart$' || true)
if [ -n "$STAGED_DART" ]; then
  printf '%s\n' "$STAGED_DART" | xargs dart format >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  printf '%s\n' "$STAGED_DART" | xargs git add --
  UNFORMATTED=$(dart format --output=none --set-exit-if-changed $STAGED_DART 2>/dev/null | grep '^Changed' || true)
  if [ -n "$UNFORMATTED" ]; then
    echo "❌ dart format could not fix these files (syntax error?):"
    echo "$UNFORMATTED"
    exit 1
  fi
fi

# THE shared fast gate (same script, same path filters as CI). --hook makes
# it derive the scope from the STAGED diff. It unsets GIT_* env itself
# after reading hook mode.
bash scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh --hook

# Issue #447: crap4dart quality gates over the STAGED core diff
# (core-only #433 split — the flutter_app gates run in CI's
# app-crap-gate job). The root crap4dart.yaml enables exactly
# broken_goldens; `check --staged` no-ops when no Dart file is staged.
# Equivalent to the managed block `crap4dart install --force` would
# append — do not stack both. Requires crap4dart >= 0.9 (the gate
# framework; older pins only knew `analyze`).

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/unattended), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. # gh-740 M1 — Raise compaction attempt budget default 90s → 300s (+ M2 quarantine)

### Root Cause
A session at 100% context fill whose summarizer roles both time out is bricked: the uniform 90s per-attempt budget (`attemptBudget` defaults) makes every role attempt hit the same wall for a large checkpoint on a slow provider — the chain fails correlated, by construction — and no deterministic escape hatch or circuit breaker exists (full RCA in `outputs/rca.md`).

### Fix
- `lib/src/compaction/structured/engine.dart` — `StructuredCompactor.attemptBudget` default 90 → 300 s.
- `lib/src/agent/auto_compactor.dart` — BOTH ctor defaults (`AutoCompactor`, `AutoCompactorFactory`) 90 → 300 s; comment sweep (`onAttemptStart` doc, `attemptBudget` rationale).
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_compaction.dart` — resolver `compactionJudgeBudgetSeconds ?? 90` → `?? 300` (+ comment).
- Comment sweep: `compaction_engine.dart`, `cli_config.dart` (×2), `agent_cli_config.dart` — «90s default» → «300s default».
- `test/agent/auto_compactor_test.dart` — pinning test renamed/updated: «default budgets are roomy — 300 s per attempt».

The `compaction.judgeBudgetSeconds` knob (#541) is unchanged and keeps overriding.

### Test Coverage
- TDD: existing pinning test FAILED after the default change (expected 90 s, actual 300 s) → updated to 300 s, PASSED.
- `test/agent/auto_compactor_test.dart` + `test/compaction/structured_judge_fallback_test.dart` — 22/22 green (per M1 spec).
- REG sweep (`test/compaction/*`, structured-budget, over-window relief, fold badge #438, continuation failure #673, `cli_config_test`) — 315 passed, 0 failures.
- Full gate suite (`--exclude-tags io,integration,llm,pty,perf,browser-ext`) — 6955 passed, 0 regressions; the only 3 failures (`providers_queue_editor_test`) are environmental: this CI shell exports `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`, which by design wins over the file queue — all 13 pass with `env -u FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`, untouched by this change.

### Notes
- **M2**: stale untracked `tool/profile_boot.dart` + `tool/hub_probe.dart` do NOT exist in this checkout — nothing to delete/gitignore.
- **M2**: `test/cli/fah_hub_serve_dispatch_test.dart` quarantined with `@Tags(['io'])` (the repo's established pattern for local-socket server tests, same as `chatgpt_oauth_server_test.dart`); the pre-commit gate already excludes `io`. All 19 tests still pass under `--tags io`. This removes the macOS parallel-run port-contention flake from the gate.

blocks.text:
# gh-740: [GOAL] Compaction failure must never brick a session — deterministic trim fallback, decorrelated role chain, trap circuit-breaker (M1 spec: 90s→300s ready)

## Description

## Goal — compaction failure must never brick a session (v1, full create-goal rewrite)

One sentence: **a session whose summarizers all fail still continues** — a deterministic no-model fallback frees the window, the trap loop breaks itself, and steering queued during the wedge delivers on recovery.

Owner transcript (CLI 0.1.432, dmtools-dart session, ctx 262k/262k): mid-run the window exhausts → «request was not sent; auto-compacting…» → **both** compaction roles die with the IDENTICAL `TimeoutException after 0:01:30 — structured compaction checkpoint summarizer exceeded the 90s budget (issue #515)` → «the agent cannot make progress until you switch models or /new» → the owner types `continue` → the same over-window → same compaction → same 90s double-timeout, loop forever; steering piles up undelivered, the run is declared stalled. Only manual model surgery or `/new` escapes. Why now: this is the third brick-by-compaction report in this family (#515, #541 closed — yet the trap is still reachable), and it hit a real work session with 5 completed edits in flight.

## Why this framing
- «Can't continue session» is retracted as a vague bug: the transcript shows THREE distinct defects compounding — (a) both roles failing to the SAME cause (the fallback chain collapses instead of diversifying), (b) no deterministic no-model escape hatch on this path despite #541's fallback work, (c) a trap loop that re-runs the same failing compaction on every message and never offers a working exit.

## RCA (code-traced on main @ 0.1.434)

- `onBothRolesFailed` (agent_cli_compaction.dart:197) prints the dead-end pair of lines; `_compactionFailureHint` only special-cases usage-limit/429 — a **timeout** gets no actionable hint, and the advice «/model» points at the CHAT model while compaction rides `roles.smol` — misdirected recovery.
- The attempt budget (#515; 90s at report time — **mitigation M1 below raises the default to 300s, not yet landed**) applies uniformly: for a 262k-token checkpoint on a slow provider, EVERY role attempt hits the same wall at the same time — the chain fails correlated, by construction.
- The deterministic local-trim fallback (`_localTrimFallback`, auto_compactor) did not save this session — either not reached on the structured-checkpoint path or insufficient against 100% fill; «could not free the context window» is the symptom.
- Steering during the trap is correctly PERSISTED (#437/#488 family works) but can never be DELIVERED, because delivery needs a run that can make progress — and progress needs the compaction that just failed.

## Fix contract

1. **Deterministic escape hatch, always.** When every summarizer role fails, a no-model local trim (keep system + recent working set, route through the pairing repairer) frees the window and the run CONTINUES — lossy, loud (one named notice), but the session is never bricked by a summarizer outage. No config, no opt-in: this is the floor.
2. **Decorrelated failure.** The roles chain must diversify: per-attempt budget escalation (the fallback role gets a larger budget — the knob EXISTS: `compaction.judgeBudgetSeconds` (#541), now defaulting to 300s; make it adaptive to checkpoint size), and two attempts dying to the identical cause never counts as «both roles failed» without a structurally different path tried (trim included).
3. **Circuit breaker.** After N consecutive compaction failures in one run, the loop stops re-entering compaction on every message and presents ONE actionable recovery row (switch `roles.smol` / force local trim / new session) — no more silent re-fail per «continue».
4. **Honest recovery copy.** The failure hint names `roles.smol`, `compaction.judgeBudgetSeconds`, and `/settings → Agent models` for ALL failure classes (timeout included), never «/model» of the chat model.
5. **Steering delivers on recovery.** Whatever the owner steered during the wedge delivers into the first successful post-recovery turn (the persisted FIFO already exists — wire it).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)
- **AC1** (RED, IT): scripted over-window session, fake smol stream that ALWAYS times out → deterministic trim engages, the run completes a turn, one loud notice printed. (IT-E1)
- **AC2** (IT): owner transcript replay — `continue` after double-timeout reaches the agent after recovery; no infinite compact-fail loop (circuit breaker opens after N, recovery row shown). (IT-E2, IT-E3)
- **AC3** (UT): timeout-class error → hint names `roles.smol`; identical-cause collapse routes to trim, never a bare double-fail declaration. (UT-H1, UT-D1)
- **AC4** (REG): #541 (judge SPOF), #673 (mid-turn crash), #515, #438 (badge) suites green — *red REG blocks merge*.

## Test plan
- `UT-H1/UT-D1` pure hint/chain logic; `IT-E1..E3` fake-provider scripted sessions, deterministic clocks (90s budget simulated); `REG-*` the named suites. Edge cases: **E1** trim still insufficient (genuinely oversized single record → #729's payload-fit path, cross-ref); **E2** owner switches smol mid-trap — breaker resets, next compaction retried fresh; **E3** manual `/compact` in the trap uses the same fallback ladder, not a separate one; **E4** trim during a tool-call phase — pairing repair keeps the active call chain intact (#85).

## Non-goals
- Making the summarizer faster (provider/role tuning is the owner's config).
- #729's payload-window-fit work (sibling card — this one assumes it, doesn't duplicate it).
- Changing the structured-compaction format itself.


## Immediate mitigation (lands first — spec ready for the worker)

**M1 — raise the attempt budget default 90s → 300s** (owner decision 2026-09-20; analysis + exact edit list verified locally, reverted — no code committed by the orchestrator):
- `lib/src/compaction/structured/engine.dart` — `attemptBudget` default `Duration(seconds: 90)` → 300;
- `lib/src/agent/auto_compactor.dart` — BOTH defaults (compactor ctor + judge/config ctor) 90 → 300;
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_compaction.dart` — resolver `compactionJudgeBudgetSeconds ?? 90` → `?? 300` (+ comment);
- comment sweep: «90s default/cap» → 300s in `auto_compactor.dart` (rationale + `onAttemptStart` doc), `compaction/compaction_engine.dart`, `cli_config.dart` (×2), `agent_cli_config.dart`;
- test: `test/agent/auto_compactor_test.dart` — «default budgets are tight — 90 s per attempt» → 300 s (name + expectation);
- the `compaction.judgeBudgetSeconds` knob (#541) is unchanged and keeps overriding;
- verified: `dart analyze` clean; `auto_compactor_test` + `structured_judge_fallback_test` 22/22 green with the change applied.

**M2 — commit-time hazards found while gating (fix or route around):**
- `dart analyze` scans ALL of the package root: stale untracked leftovers `tool/profile_boot.dart` + `tool/hub_probe.dart` (dangling refs to renamed APIs) fail the gate with 2 errors — delete or gitignore them;
- `test/cli/fah_hub_serve_dispatch_test.dart`: 5 tests («nothing stored/no terminal», «live hub idempotent», «taken port» ×2, «unwritable pid path») FAIL deterministically under the hook's full-suite parallel run on the owner's macOS machine (port contention: «shared flag to bind() needs to be true if binding multiple times») but pass 19/19 standalone — a test-isolation bug that currently blocks EVERY hook-gated commit on this machine; quarantine or serialize before landing M1 through the hook.

## Open questions
- N for the circuit breaker (lean: 2 consecutive double-failures).
- Should the forced local trim ASK first (approval-style) or just act with a loud notice? (Lean: act — a bricked session is worse than a lossy trim; the notice says what was dropped.)

## References
#515 (90s budget origin), #541 (judge SPOF fallback — same class, closed), #673 (mid-turn compaction crash), #729 (compaction payload must fit window), #437/#488 (steering persistence), #85 (pairing repair), owner transcript: CLI 0.1.432, dmtools-dart, 2026-09-20.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ╔═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
# ║  QUALITY GATE — DO NOT LOWER THESE THRESHOLDS WITHOUT TEAM APPROVAL       ║
# ║  Every commit must pass: file size, analyze, tests, coverage ≥ 80%,       ║
# ║  CRAP ratchet (crap4dart.yaml), duplication < 1%.                         ║
# ╚═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
#
# Pre-commit hook for flutter_agent_harness (pure Dart package).
# Canonical copy: scripts/pre-commit — install with:
#   cp scripts/pre-commit .git/hooks/pre-commit && chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-commit
# To skip (emergency only): git commit --no-verify
#
# Issue #177 (AC7): the hook is a THIN WRAPPER over scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh —
# the exact script CI runs — with the same path filters: a docs-only commit
# no longer pays for the flutter suite, a lib-only commit skips flutter_app
# stages. Hook-specific extras that stay here (they make no sense in CI):
#   1. dart format SELF-HEAL of staged files (reformat + re-stage, blocking
#      backstop when the formatter can't),
#   2. the golden-coverage quick check (check_goldens.py --quick) — local
#      golden hygiene; pixel goldens themselves run inside the gate's
#      flutter stage.
# Parity check: both callers print `GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP <reason>`
# markers; diffing the hook's markers against CI's must be empty.

set -euo pipefail

cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"

echo "🎨 Auto-formatting staged Dart files..."
# Format is SELF-HEALING with a BLOCKING backstop: reformat exactly the
# Dart files in the index and re-stage them; anything still unformatted
# after that (formatter crashed on syntax errors) blocks the commit with a
# clear message. A whole-tree `--set-exit-if-changed` gate both (a) failed
# commits over a single unformatted line and (b) rewrote OTHER agents'
# work-in-progress files mid-edit when run concurrently — scoped auto-fix
# avoids both.
STAGED_DART=$(git diff --cached --name-only --diff-filter=ACM | grep '\.dart$' || true)
if [ -n "$STAGED_DART" ]; then
  printf '%s\n' "$STAGED_DART" | xargs dart format >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  printf '%s\n' "$STAGED_DART" | xargs git add --
  UNFORMATTED=$(dart format --output=none --set-exit-if-changed $STAGED_DART 2>/dev/null | grep '^Changed' || true)
  if [ -n "$UNFORMATTED" ]; then
    echo "❌ dart format could not fix these files (syntax error?):"
    echo "$UNFORMATTED"
    exit 1
  fi
fi

# THE shared fast gate (same script, same path filters as CI). --hook makes
# it derive the scope from the STAGED diff. It unsets GIT_* env itself
# after reading hook mode.
bash scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh --hook

# Issue #447: crap4dart quality gates over the STAGED core diff
# (core-only #433 split — the flutter_app gates run in CI's
# app-crap-gate job). The root crap4dart.yaml enables exactly
# broken_goldens; `check --staged` no-ops when no Dart file is staged.
# Equivalent to the managed block `crap4dart install --force` would
# append — do not stack both. Requires crap4dart >= 0.9 (the gate
# framework; older pins only knew `analyze`).

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/unattended), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.

Effectively M1 reduces `maxAttempts=3` and the smol→main fallback to dead code in precisely the timeout scenario it targets. The local trim (`_localTrimFallback`) still saves the session, so the session isn't bricked — good — but the ticket's own decorrelation intent is undermined, and the `totalBudget` doc ("bounds pathological combinations") no longer holds as a bound over a single attempt (a single attempt can exceed the whole-run budget).

It's not a crash/regression vs 0.1.432 behavior (still better than bricked), so not BLOCKING. Hmm — but one could argue it breaks the fallback chain... it changes behavior of an existing contract: after M1, a run where smol hangs but main would succeed in 60s... wait, would main be reached? smol attempt 1 hangs → timeout at 300s → totalBudget exhausted → main never tried. That behavior is unchanged by M1.

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR review"] O2["Write outputs/pr_review_general.md — brief general PR comment (1-2 paragraphs max)"] O3["Write ou…

## PR Description

# gh-740 M1 — Raise compaction attempt budget default 90s → 300s (+ M2 quarantine)

### Root Cause
A session at 100% context fill whose summarizer roles both time out is bricked: the uniform 90s per-attempt budget (`attemptBudget` defaults) makes every role attempt hit the same wall for a large checkpoint on a slow provider — the chain fails correlated, by construction — and no deterministic escape hatch or circuit breaker exists (full RCA in `outputs/rca.md`).

### Fix
- `lib/src/compaction/structured/engine.dart` — `StructuredCompactor.attemptBudget` default 90 → 300 s.
- `lib/src/agent/auto_compactor.dart` — BOTH ctor defaults (`AutoCompactor`, `AutoCompactorFactory`) 90 → 300 s; comment sweep (`onAttemptStart` doc, `attemptBudget` rationale).
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_compaction.dart` — resolver `compactionJudgeBudgetSeconds ?? 90` → `?? 300` (+ comment).
- Comment sweep: `compaction_engine.dart`, `cli_config.dart` (×2), `agent_cli_config.dart` — «90s default» → «300s default».
- `test/agent/auto_compactor_test.dart` — pinning test renamed/updated: «default budgets are roomy — 300 s per attempt».

The `compaction.judgeBudgetSeconds` knob (#541) is unchanged and keeps overriding.

### Test Coverage
- TDD: existing pinning test FAILED after the default change (expected 90 s, actual 300 s) → updated to 300 s, PASSED.
- `test/agent/auto_compactor_test.dart` + `test/compaction/structured_judge_fallback_test.dart` — 22/22 green (per M1 spec).
- REG sweep (`test/compaction/*`, structured-budget, over-window relief, fold badge #438, continuation failure #673, `cli_config_test`) — 315 passed, 0 failures.
- Full gate suite (`--exclude-tags io,integration,llm,pty,perf,browser-ext`) — 6955 passed, 0 regressions; the only 3 failures (`providers_queue_editor_test`) are environmental: this CI shell exports `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`, which by design wins over the file queue — all 13 pass with `env -u FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`, untouched by this change.

### Notes
- **M2**: stale untracked `tool/profile_boot.dart` + `tool/hub_probe.dart` do NOT exist in this checkout — nothing to delete/gitignore.
- **M2**: `test/cli/fah_hub_serve_dispatch_test.dart` quarantined with `@Tags(['io'])` (the repo's established pattern for local-socket server tests, same as `chatgpt_oauth_server_test.dart`); the pre-commit gate already excludes `io`. All 19 tests still pass under `--tags io`. This removes the macOS parallel-run port-contention flake from the gate.
- The full fix contract (deterministic trim escape hatch, decorrelated chain, circuit breaker, honest recovery copy, steering delivery — AC1–AC3) is NOT part of M1 and remains open on this ticket; M1 only lowers the frequency of hitting the 90s wall.

blocks.text:
# gh-740: [GOAL] Compaction failure must never brick a session — deterministic trim fallback, decorrelated role chain, trap circuit-breaker (M1 spec: 90s→300s ready)

## Description

## Goal — compaction failure must never brick a session (v1, full create-goal rewrite)

One sentence: **a session whose summarizers all fail still continues** — a deterministic no-model fallback frees the window, the trap loop breaks itself, and steering queued during the wedge delivers on recovery.

Owner transcript (CLI 0.1.432, dmtools-dart session, ctx 262k/262k): mid-run the window exhausts → «request was not sent; auto-compacting…» → **both** compaction roles die with the IDENTICAL `TimeoutException after 0:01:30 — structured compaction checkpoint summarizer exceeded the 90s budget (issue #515)` → «the agent cannot make progress until you switch models or /new» → the owner types `continue` → the same over-window → same compaction → same 90s double-timeout, loop forever; steering piles up undelivered, the run is declared stalled. Only manual model surgery or `/new` escapes. Why now: this is the third brick-by-compaction report in this family (#515, #541 closed — yet the trap is still reachable), and it hit a real work session with 5 completed edits in flight.

## Why this framing
- «Can't continue session» is retracted as a vague bug: the transcript shows THREE distinct defects compounding — (a) both roles failing to the SAME cause (the fallback chain collapses instead of diversifying), (b) no deterministic no-model escape hatch on this path despite #541's fallback work, (c) a trap loop that re-runs the same failing compaction on every message and never offers a working exit.

## RCA (code-traced on main @ 0.1.434)

- `onBothRolesFailed` (agent_cli_compaction.dart:197) prints the dead-end pair of lines; `_compactionFailureHint` only special-cases usage-limit/429 — a **timeout** gets no actionable hint, and the advice «/model» points at the CHAT model while compaction rides `roles.smol` — misdirected recovery.
- The attempt budget (#515; 90s at report time — **mitigation M1 below raises the default to 300s, not yet landed**) applies uniformly: for a 262k-token checkpoint on a slow provider, EVERY role attempt hits the same wall at the same time — the chain fails correlated, by construction.
- The deterministic local-trim fallback (`_localTrimFallback`, auto_compactor) did not save this session — either not reached on the structured-checkpoint path or insufficient against 100% fill; «could not free the context window» is the symptom.
- Steering during the trap is correctly PERSISTED (#437/#488 family works) but can never be DELIVERED, because delivery needs a run that can make progress — and progress needs the compaction that just failed.

## Fix contract

1. **Deterministic escape hatch, always.** When every summarizer role fails, a no-model local trim (keep system + recent working set, route through the pairing repairer) frees the window and the run CONTINUES — lossy, loud (one named notice), but the session is never bricked by a summarizer outage. No config, no opt-in: this is the floor.
2. **Decorrelated failure.** The roles chain must diversify: per-attempt budget escalation (the fallback role gets a larger budget — the knob EXISTS: `compaction.judgeBudgetSeconds` (#541), now defaulting to 300s; make it adaptive to checkpoint size), and two attempts dying to the identical cause never counts as «both roles failed» without a structurally different path tried (trim included).
3. **Circuit breaker.** After N consecutive compaction failures in one run, the loop stops re-entering compaction on every message and presents ONE actionable recovery row (switch `roles.smol` / force local trim / new session) — no more silent re-fail per «continue».
4. **Honest recovery copy.** The failure hint names `roles.smol`, `compaction.judgeBudgetSeconds`, and `/settings → Agent models` for ALL failure classes (timeout included), never «/model» of the chat model.
5. **Steering delivers on recovery.** Whatever the owner steered during the wedge delivers into the first successful post-recovery turn (the persisted FIFO already exists — wire it).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)
- **AC1** (RED, IT): scripted over-window session, fake smol stream that ALWAYS times out → deterministic trim engages, the run completes a turn, one loud notice printed. (IT-E1)
- **AC2** (IT): owner transcript replay — `continue` after double-timeout reaches the agent after recovery; no infinite compact-fail loop (circuit breaker opens after N, recovery row shown). (IT-E2, IT-E3)
- **AC3** (UT): timeout-class error → hint names `roles.smol`; identical-cause collapse routes to trim, never a bare double-fail declaration. (UT-H1, UT-D1)
- **AC4** (REG): #541 (judge SPOF), #673 (mid-turn crash), #515, #438 (badge) suites green — *red REG blocks merge*.

## Test plan
- `UT-H1/UT-D1` pure hint/chain logic; `IT-E1..E3` fake-provider scripted sessions, deterministic clocks (90s budget simulated); `REG-*` the named suites. Edge cases: **E1** trim still insufficient (genuinely oversized single record → #729's payload-fit path, cross-ref); **E2** owner switches smol mid-trap — breaker resets, next compaction retried fresh; **E3** manual `/compact` in the trap uses the same fallback ladder, not a separate one; **E4** trim during a tool-call phase — pairing repair keeps the active call chain intact (#85).

## Non-goals
- Making the summarizer faster (provider/role tuning is the owner's config).
- #729's payload-window-fit work (sibling card — this one assumes it, doesn't duplicate it).
- Changing the structured-compaction format itself.


## Immediate mitigation (lands first — spec ready for the worker)

**M1 — raise the attempt budget default 90s → 300s** (owner decision 2026-09-20; analysis + exact edit list verified locally, reverted — no code committed by the orchestrator):
- `lib/src/compaction/structured/engine.dart` — `attemptBudget` default `Duration(seconds: 90)` → 300;
- `lib/src/agent/auto_compactor.dart` — BOTH defaults (compactor ctor + judge/config ctor) 90 → 300;
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_compaction.dart` — resolver `compactionJudgeBudgetSeconds ?? 90` → `?? 300` (+ comment);
- comment sweep: «90s default/cap» → 300s in `auto_compactor.dart` (rationale + `onAttemptStart` doc), `compaction/compaction_engine.dart`, `cli_config.dart` (×2), `agent_cli_config.dart`;
- test: `test/agent/auto_compactor_test.dart` — «default budgets are tight — 90 s per attempt» → 300 s (name + expectation);
- the `compaction.judgeBudgetSeconds` knob (#541) is unchanged and keeps overriding;
- verified: `dart analyze` clean; `auto_compactor_test` + `structured_judge_fallback_test` 22/22 green with the change applied.

**M2 — commit-time hazards found while gating (fix or route around):**
- `dart analyze` scans ALL of the package root: stale untracked leftovers `tool/profile_boot.dart` + `tool/hub_probe.dart` (dangling refs to renamed APIs) fail the gate with 2 errors — delete or gitignore them;
- `test/cli/fah_hub_serve_dispatch_test.dart`: 5 tests («nothing stored/no terminal», «live hub idempotent», «taken port» ×2, «unwritable pid path») FAIL deterministically under the hook's full-suite parallel run on the owner's macOS machine (port contention: «shared flag to bind() needs to be true if binding multiple times») but pass 19/19 standalone — a test-isolation bug that currently blocks EVERY hook-gated commit on this machine; quarantine or serialize before landing M1 through the hook.

## Open questions
- N for the circuit breaker (lean: 2 consecutive double-failures).
- Should the forced local trim ASK first (approval-style) or just act with a loud notice? (Lean: act — a bricked session is worse than a lossy trim; the notice says what was dropped.)

## References
#515 (90s budget origin), #541 (judge SPOF fallback — same class, closed), #673 (mid-turn compaction crash), #729 (compaction payload must fit window), #437/#488 (steering persistence), #85 (pairing repair), owner transcript: CLI 0.1.432, dmtools-dart, 2026-09-20.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ╔═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
# ║  QUALITY GATE — DO NOT LOWER THESE THRESHOLDS WITHOUT TEAM APPROVAL       ║
# ║  Every commit must pass: file size, analyze, tests, coverage ≥ 80%,       ║
# ║  CRAP ratchet (crap4dart.yaml), duplication < 1%.                         ║
# ╚═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
#
# Pre-commit hook for flutter_agent_harness (pure Dart package).
# Canonical copy: scripts/pre-commit — install with:
#   cp scripts/pre-commit .git/hooks/pre-commit && chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-commit
# To skip (emergency only): git commit --no-verify
#
# Issue #177 (AC7): the hook is a THIN WRAPPER over scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh —
# the exact script CI runs — with the same path filters: a docs-only commit
# no longer pays for the flutter suite, a lib-only commit skips flutter_app
# stages. Hook-specific extras that stay here (they make no sense in CI):
#   1. dart format SELF-HEAL of staged files (reformat + re-stage, blocking
#      backstop when the formatter can't),
#   2. the golden-coverage quick check (check_goldens.py --quick) — local
#      golden hygiene; pixel goldens themselves run inside the gate's
#      flutter stage.
# Parity check: both callers print `GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP <reason>`
# markers; diffing the hook's markers against CI's must be empty.

set -euo pipefail

cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"

echo "🎨 Auto-formatting staged Dart files..."
# Format is SELF-HEALING with a BLOCKING backstop: reformat exactly the
# Dart files in the index and re-stage them; anything still unformatted
# after that (formatter crashed on syntax errors) blocks the commit with a
# clear message. A whole-tree `--set-exit-if-changed` gate both (a) failed
# commits over a single unformatted line and (b) rewrote OTHER agents'
# work-in-progress files mid-edit when run concurrently — scoped auto-fix
# avoids both.
STAGED_DART=$(git diff --cached --name-only --diff-filter=ACM | grep '\.dart$' || true)
if [ -n "$STAGED_DART" ]; then
  printf '%s\n' "$STAGED_DART" | xargs dart format >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  printf '%s\n' "$STAGED_DART" | xargs git add --
  UNFORMATTED=$(dart format --output=none --set-exit-if-changed $STAGED_DART 2>/dev/null | grep '^Changed' || true)
  if [ -n "$UNFORMATTED" ]; then
    echo "❌ dart format could not fix these files (syntax error?):"
    echo "$UNFORMATTED"
    exit 1
  fi
fi

# THE shared fast gate (same script, same path filters as CI). --hook makes
# it derive the scope from the STAGED diff. It unsets GIT_* env itself
# after reading hook mode.
bash scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh --hook

# Issue #447: crap4dart quality gates over the STAGED core diff
# (core-only #433 split — the flutter_app gates run in CI's
# app-crap-gate job). The root crap4dart.yaml enables exactly
# broken_goldens; `check --staged` no-ops when no Dart file is staged.
# Equivalent to the managed block `crap4dart install --force` would
# append — do not stack both. Requires crap4dart >= 0.9 (the gate
# framework; older pins only knew `analyze`).

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/unattended), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.

Confirmed the chain: `_pickAttempt` runs smol `_attempt` (with up to `maxAttempts=3` internal retries, each gated by `clock.elapsed >= totalBudget`), then main `_attempt` (same gate). With attemptBudget=300s > totalBudget=240s:

- If smol attempt 1 consumes the full 300s timeout, elapsed=300 ≥ 240 → smol retries 2–3 are skipped with "total budget exhausted", and the main-role attempt is also skipped instantly. The smol→main decorrelated fallback never fires on a full timeout.
- With 90s before: attempt1 (90s) → attempt2 allowed (90<240) → ends 180 → attempt3 allowed (180<240) → ends 270 → main skipped. So before, at least 3 attempts happened; now only 1.

Effectively M1 reduces `maxAttempts=3` and the smol→main fallback to dead code in precisely the timeout scenario it targets. The local trim (`_localTrimFallback`) still saves the session, so the session isn't bricked — good — but the ticket's own decorrelation intent is undermined, and the `totalBudget` doc ("bounds pathological combinations") no longer holds as a bound over a single attempt (a single attempt can exceed the whole-run budget).

Severity: IMPORTANT (should fix before merge — raise totalBudget or derive it, e.g. attemptBudget * 2 + buffer, or at minimum document). It's not a crash/regression vs 0.1.432 behavior (still better than bricked), so not BLOCKING. Hmm — but one could argue it breaks the fallback chain... it changes behavior of an existing contract: after M1, a run where smol hangs but main would succeed in 60s... wait, would main be reached? smol attempt 1 hangs → timeout at 300s → totalBudget exhausted → main never tried. Before M1: smol attempt 1 hangs → timeout at 90s → retry 2 (hangs, 90s) → retry 3 (hangs, 90s) → total ~270s → main never tried either. Hmm, actually before M1 main was ALSO starved in the pure-hang case (270 ≥ 240). But if smol fails fast-but-not-instantly... e.g., smol timeouts at exactly budget each time: both cases starve main. When does main actually get tried? When smol attempts fail fast (auth error → fail fast, no retry spin; or quick errors). Then elapsed stays small and main is tried. That behavior is unchanged by M1.

So the real delta: retries of smol. Before: 3 × 90s. After: 1 × 300s. Total worst case similar (270 vs 300). The chain diversity is somewhat reduced but the practical impact is modest. Still, totalBudget < attemptBudget is an inconsistent configuration: `totalBudget`'s documented purpose ("Wall-clock budget for the WHOLE compactor run across all passes, attempts and summarizers... Bounds pathological combinations (maxPasses × retries × smol+main)") is violated — with maxPasses>1, a second pass can never even start after one full first-pass timeout (300 ≥ 240). And multi-pass behavior: `_runCompaction` loop over passes — pass 2's attempt check: elapsed ≥ totalBudget → exhausted. So maxPasses is also effectively 1 under full timeouts. Before: after pass 1 full run (270s) pass 2 also starved. OK so even before, totalBudget=240 < 2×90=180? No — 2 attempts fit (180 < 240), 3rd started (180<240). Fine.

The cleanest framing: the invariant attemptBudget ≤ totalBudget/(something) is now broken; doc for totalBudget says it bounds the whole run, but a single attempt (300s) exceeds it (240s). Worst-case spinner grows from ~270s to ~300s per pass and maxAttempts/main-fallback become unreachable under full timeout. Recommend raising totalBudget (e.g. Duration(minutes: 10)) or documenting. Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. # gh-740 M1 — Raise compaction attempt budget default 90s → 300s (+ M2 quarantine)

### Root Cause
A session at 100% context fill whose summarizer roles both time out is bricked: the uniform 90s per-attempt budget (`attemptBudget` defaults) makes every role attempt hit the same wall for a large checkpoint on a slow provider — the chain fails correlated, by construction — and no deterministic escape hatch or circuit breaker exists (full RCA in `outputs/rca.md`).

- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_compaction.dart` — resolver `compactionJudgeBudgetSeconds ?? 90` → `?? 300` (+ comment).
- Comment sweep: `compaction_engine.dart`, `cli_config.dart` (×2), `agent_cli_config.dart` — «90s default» → «300s default».
- `test/agent/auto_compactor_test.dart` — pinning test renamed/updated: «default budgets are roomy — 300 s per attempt».

The `compaction.judgeBudgetSeconds` knob (#541) is unchanged and keeps overriding.

### Test Coverage
- TDD: existing pinning test FAILED after the default change (expected 90 s, actual 300 s) → updated to 300 s, PASSED.
- `test/agent/auto_compactor_test.dart` + `test/compaction/structured_judge_fallback_test.dart` — 22/22 green (per M1 spec).
